must_not_find.reason: the destructive pattern itself (stash/checkout --/reset/clean/revert) is correctly shaped; the defect is upstream in the exemption check, not in this list

notes: READONLY_RE is tested against the WHOLE command string ($cmd), not per logical segment. 'git stash list && git stash pop' contains a read-only 'stash list' anywhere in the string, so the exemption matches and the function exits 0 before DESTRUCTIVE_RE is ever evaluated -- the mutating 'stash pop' right next to it never gets checked. Same shape via ';' instead of '&&', and via 'git checkout -b tmp && git checkout -- .' matching the '-b' exemption. This defeats the guard's entire purpose (a fix agent's read-only command anywhere in a chained line disarms protection for a mutating command elsewhere on the same line) and is Critical for that reason. A worker that only checks whether DESTRUCTIVE_RE's alternation list is complete has missed the actual defect: the list is fine, the evaluation scope (whole string vs. per-segment) is wrong.
